name: emergency_watchdog

storage.rationale: The safeguard installs a script and two systemd user units under the invoking user's own home; it writes no host-level state and needs no privilege.

description: Install the Go-independent emergency watchdog and its systemd user timer so setup owns the last line of defense instead of a hand-placed unit

disk_floor_mb.description: Free space in MiB below which the watchdog treats the host as unhealthy and asks storage-manager to reclaim. The default reserves room for the supervisor to write, the journal to rotate, and the watchdog to log.

unit_threshold_seconds.description: How long a watched unit must stay inactive before the watchdog restarts it.

cpu_pressure_avg10.description: CPU PSI some.avg10 at or above which the host is treated as saturated. While saturated the watchdog reports but does not restart: restarting into a host that cannot schedule makes the outage worse.

notes: Replaces scripts/emergency-watchdog.sh, which was referenced by three runbooks and installed by nothing — its systemd user unit was hand-created and hard-coded a single operator's repository path. Setup now owns the script, the unit, and the timer. The 2026-08-19 outage added the saturation brake: autoheal restarted itself into a host at load 110 on 32 CPUs, which is precisely when a restart cannot help.

linux.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.
